text:
emily-support: FYI QuasarTech's dedicated pool qz-prod-ded1 is getting a sustained burst and we're seeing token-per-second SLO violations + 429s since about 09:12 UTC. Customer reports timeouts and higher latencies.
emily-support: Their traffic pattern: short spikes every 30s for ~90s, sustained for ~40m. Burst credits dropped to 0 within the first 5m.
anita-customer-success: Quasar says this started right after a marketing email — they expected a burst but thought reserved capacity would cover it. They're unhappy about 429s.
jordan-eng: Can you paste the admission controller logs and a request sample? Need to confirm whether credits are being consumed by prefix cache misses or admission gating.
emily-support: Pasting relevant snippets: 
```
[09:12:03] admission: pool=qz-prod-ded1 request_id=abcd1234 auth=ok tps=3200 tokens=4 admit=false reason=burst_credits_exhausted remaining=0
[09:12:09] admission: pool=qz-prod-ded1 request_id=abcd5678 admit=false reason=throttle_queue_len=256
[09:13:10] autoscale: pool=qz-prod-ded1 pods=8->8 recommended=12 cooldown=120s
```
lee-sre: Autoscaler recommendation being ignored because pool is marked as "no-autoscale" for reserve stability. That explains why node count didn't grow automatically.
sam-ops: Confirmed: budgeting config for qz-prod-ded1 has autoscale disabled. They bought a fixed reserved pool — but burst credits should cover short spikes; here spikes are long enough to deplete credits.
maria-ml: What model and sequence lengths? If avg seq len is high, token drain is much faster.
emily-support: Quasar is running a medium LLM with avg seq tokens ~120. That increases token/s consumption vs our baseline.
jordan-eng: Two parts: (1) customer-facing mitigation: route ~30% of burst traffic to their hosted fallback model (lower cost, more throughput) or enable temporary autoscale; (2) platform fix: make burst refill aggressive for sustained 10m spikes or allow emergency prewarm. Which options are available now?
anita-customer-success: Quasar asked for a short-term toggle to increase headroom. They want a plan and ETA.
sam-ops: We can manually add two extra GPU instances (prewarm) within ~7-10 minutes if approved by finance. That will increase admission headroom.
lee-sre: Quick repro steps I ran:
```
# simulate burst
ab -n 10000 -c 200 -p small_payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=qz-medium
# admission logs show credits drop to 0 in ~3m with seq_len=120
```
jordan-eng: Also noted an auth retry pattern from same tenant that causes small extra load due to 401->retry loop. Need to check their SDK.
emily-support: Customer said they saw intermittent 401s right after the campaign. Could be token churn on their side. I've asked them to report SDK logs.
maria-ml: Suggest lowering per-request token ceiling via per-route config to limit worst-case drain during bursts. E.g., max_tokens=64 on non-critical routes.
anita-customer-success: I'll suggest that as a quick mitigation while we scale. Quasar approved a manual prewarm for 2 GPUs. Please proceed.
sam-ops: Kicked off prewarm request: `runbook: prewarm_pool qz-prod-ded1 add=2 reason=customer-escalation` — waiting on deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Prewarm job submitted for pool qz-prod-ded1, job=prewarm-2765432118, eta=8m.
lee-sre: After prewarm completes, we should monitor admission: `curl -s https://ops.redwood.ai/pools/qz-prod-ded1/metrics | jq .admission` and watch `burst_credits` and `throttle_reject_rate`.
jordan-eng: Long-term: need a policy change — for reserved pools that disable autoscale, implement an "emergency headroom override" that can be enabled by support with audit + billing notif. Also enhance our arrival model so burst credit refill is not the only lever.
emily-support: Customer is OK with manual prewarm now. I'll send them the mitigation and ask for SDK logs for the 401s. Keeping this thread for updates.
lee-sre: Note — file a follow-up ticket for product to evaluate: increase default refill rate for same-customer sustained bursts above 5m and add an alert when recommended pods > current pods by 30%.
anita-customer-success: Quasar appreciates the quick response. They're sampling requests to evaluate fallback quality.
emily-support: Last check: at 09:24 UTC after prewarm started, admission rejects dropped from 18%->2%. Monitoring to 09:34.
emily-support: (closing if stable)
